answer: A staking bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock tokens before it can trade, like planting a vine in a garden — cheap to start, costly to fake at scale. An attacker creating thousands of clones must fund every one, and slashing burns the bond of any identity caught lying. Honest agents earn the bond back through real work, while a Sybil farm faces a dune of costs that grows with every fake account it adds.
